text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Add a single high-contrast skip link at the top of every page that only appears when focused. This guarantees keyboard users can bypass repetitive navigation blocks in one keystroke, fixing the biggest keyboard trap in EXCAVA. The trade-off is a small visual cue that briefly shifts layout when tabbed to, but it’s the only way to meet WCAG 2.2 Level A and avoid frustrating users who rely on keyboards.

name: Reader
text: The real risk is that the persistent skip link may still go unnoticed, blending into the design and not effectively serving its purpose. Instead, consider implementing clear visual distinction—like a contrasting background color that activates when focused—making it harder to overlook. To settle the argument, we could conduct user testing with keyboard-only navigators to see whether they can reliably find and use the skip link as it currently stands.

name: Ramp
text:
Add a **high-contrast skip link** that appears *only* when focused, with a bold outline and a bright background that doesn’t shift layout. This ensures keyboard users can bypass blocks instantly without visual clutter for mouse users. The trade-off is a brief, intentional layout shift when the link appears—but that’s the point: it’s a deliberate signal, not noise.

name: Reader
text: The real risk is that a high-contrast skip link still risks blending into the page if the contrast isn’t *exactly* right—users may miss it even when focused. Instead, make it a full-width bar at the top of the page that appears on focus, ensuring it’s impossible to overlook. Settle this by testing with keyboard users in real conditions.
